title: The Broken Summit
premise: Casper Okafor, a mountain guide blacklisted from Nepal and Peru after a summit expedition ended in a client's death she swears wasn't her fault, scrapes by running river trips in the lawless borderlands of the Karakoram. When her old rival Devlin Marsh arrives with a permit for the forbidden Keshar Concession and a crew of misfits, Casper takes the job to pay off the debt keeping her exiled from her daughter. Mid-expedition they discover Marsh's permits are forged and his real cargo is evidence that could expose the mining syndicate responsible for the death that ruined her—forcing Casper to choose between finishing the job and turning back through monsoon floods with a leaking boat, a stranger named Ilsa who knows too much, and the truth everyone swore off long ago. The novel ends with Casper delivering the evidence not to authorities but to the mountain villages themselves, clearing her name at the cost of her license forever, and choosing the found family of her crew over the official redemption she once wanted.
about_author: Tamsin Okafor is a former expedition cook who spent eleven seasons in high-altitude base camps before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories from a converted school bus that follows the climbing season across three continents.

chapters.title: The River Keeps No Records
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Running an illegal ferry crossing on the Indus tributaries, Casper patches leaks both literal and financial while dodging a patrol boat. A letter arrives: her daughter's tuition is due, and the debt collector wants payment in sixty days. Emotional beat: exhaustion masked as competence; the cost of invisibility made concrete.

chapters.title: A Ghost with Good Credit
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Devlin Marsh walks into the riverside tea house where Casper hides out, offering triple rate for a guide who can read water no one else can. She refuses; he leaves the permit on the table anyway. Flashback fragments of the disaster on Nanda Kot surface unbidden. Emotional beat: old shame meeting old rivalry.

chapters.title: Sixty Days of Bad Options
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She audits her crew—Tomas the mechanic, Priya the medic, young Ferro who idolizes her—and realizes none of them will survive another season without pay. She signs Marsh's contract at midnight, telling herself it's just money. Emotional beat: self-deception crystallizing into commitment.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Reads Currents
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Introduced as Marsh's hydrologist, Ilsa boards with instruments Casper doesn't recognize and questions that feel like interrogations. On the first night she quietly re-rigs Casper's boat, saving it from a hidden sandbar. Emotional beat: wary respect between two women who both hide things well.

chapters.title: Upstream of Everything
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The crew pushes into the gorge system toward the Keshar headwaters. Marsh reveals the route skirts the exact valley where Casper's career died. Priya notices Casper's hands shaking at the tiller. Emotional beat: the past geography refusing to stay past.

chapters.title: What the Permit Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa discovers the concession paperwork is stamped with dates that haven't occurred yet—forged, and recently. She photographs everything but tells no one, testing whether Casper is complicit or a mark. Emotional beat: loneliness of carrying knowledge you can't yet share.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Clouds stack over the ridgeline two weeks early. Marsh insists they push on; Casper calculates they have four days before the gorges flood. First open argument between them, witnessed by the whole crew. Emotional beat: leadership under pressure, authority contested.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers Her Name
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Resupply stop at Serkhang, where survivors of the Nanda Kot expedition live. An old woman spits at Casper's feet; a boy asks if she's the one who 'let the mountain eat his father.' Casper learns the dead client was investigating the mine upstream. Emotional beat: grief weaponized against her, doubt taking root.

chapters.title: Cargo in the Dry Boxes
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro, snooping for cigarettes, finds sealed cases of core samples and documents marked with the syndicate's logo. He tells Priya; together they confront Ilsa, who admits the job is evidence extraction, not surveying. Emotional beat: betrayal rippling down the hierarchy of trust.

chapters.title: Mutiny at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The crew demands answers at the river junction. Marsh confesses partially: the samples prove the mine poisoned the watershed and caused the rockfall that killed Casper's client. He needs Casper because only she knows the escape route. Emotional beat: rage and revelation braided together; the sworn-off job revealed.

chapters.title: The Route Nobody Swore Off Twice
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Alone at night, Casper maps the flooded gorge route from memory—the one she swore never to run again after Nanda Kot. She realizes the disaster may have been sabotage, not her error. Emotional beat: the architecture of guilt beginning to collapse.

chapters.title: First Water Over the Gunwales
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The monsoon hits early. The boat takes on water in the first rapids; Tomas's patchwork holds by meters. Ilsa saves the sample cases over the fuel, forcing a choice that strands their reserve power. Emotional beat: crisis stripping pretense; competence becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: Two Women, One Bilge Pump
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Night camp in a sea cave. Ilsa tells Casper her brother died in the mine's collapse—she's been hunting this evidence for six years. Casper admits she suspected but ran instead of fighting. They agree, without ceremony, to finish it together. Emotional beat: love against duty, chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: Marsh's Second Boat
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro spots a second vessel shadowing them—syndicate security, hired when Marsh's forgery was detected. Marsh tries to negotiate alone and comes back bleeding. The crew realizes they're now witnesses, not contractors. Emotional beat: the point of no return crossed in blood.

chapters.title: The Portage of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. They abandon the main channel and portage gear over a landslide scar, Casper leading on routes her body remembers better than her mind. Priya treats Marsh's wounds; he finally apologizes for Nanda Kot—he sold the route to the syndicate years ago. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered but not yet accepted.

chapters.title: Permits Expiring
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Radio contact: the concession window closes in three days, and syndicate lawyers are moving to have the entire crew declared criminals—like her. Casper understands the trap: deliver the evidence illegally and stay blacklisted forever, or quit and let it burn. Emotional beat: duty and justice pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Gorge That Forgives Nothing
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The final gorge run at peak flood. The pursuing boat capsizes behind them; Casper turns back against every instinct to pull two drowning security men aboard. Ilsa watches her do it and understands who Casper actually is. Emotional beat: character revealed under maximum pressure.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Truce with the soaked, humbled security men. At the mine's outflow, the crew sees the poisoned water firsthand. Casper names the dead aloud—her client, Ilsa's brother, the village fathers. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: Deliverance, Illegally
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Climax begins: they must move the evidence through the last checkpoint before the permit expires, with syndicate agents waiting. Casper devises the impossible route—the one from her nightmares—as a decoy while Ilsa carries copies overland to Serkhang. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Broken Summit
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Climax. Casper runs the nightmare gorge solo as bait, nearly dies, and is pulled from the water by Ferro and the reformed security men. Marsh sacrifices his own escape to draw the agents off, disappearing downstream. Emotional beat: the title earned—summits broken open into something truer than conquest.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. In Serkhang, the evidence is read aloud to the village assembly; the syndicate's lease collapses under international exposure. Casper's name is cleared in the valley but not in any court—her blacklist stands. She chooses the villages' verdict over the state's. Emotional beat: justice achieved outside every system that failed her.

chapters.title: Downstream, Together
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Epilogue. Weeks later, the patched boat runs tourists—not summiteers—down safe waters. Ilsa stays; the debt is paid; Casper writes to her daughter with the truth enclosed. The wilderness still forgives nothing, but she has stopped asking it to. Emotional beat: found family secured, exile reframed as homecoming.
